result.summary: The image shows a residential street corner lacking basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps. A large vehicle parked close to the corner creates a significant visual obstruction for both pedestrians and drivers at the intersection.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A black SUV is parked directly at the corner, blocking sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, parked at the curb near the corner.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Infrastructure
hazards.description: Absence of marked crosswalks and curb ramps makes the crossing less safe and inaccessible for people with mobility impairments.
hazards.location_in_image: The intersection area in the foreground.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalk markings and ADA-compliant curb ramps to define pedestrian space and ensure accessibility.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a sidewalk separated from the roadway by a narrow grass strip and fencing. There is a lack of marked pedestrian crossings, traffic control devices, or curb ramps, and parked vehicles along the curb create potential sightline obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line can block the visibility between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street along the curb.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated or marked crossing points are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross in unmarked areas without priority.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, curb ramps, and marked crosswalks at a signalized junction. However, the crosswalk markings are significantly faded and the lack of visible pedestrian-specific signals or curb extensions increases exposure risk in this residential area.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk markings in the foreground are heavily worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection may block sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Pavement degradation
hazards.description: Cracking and wear in the asphalt within the crosswalk area present a minor trip hazard.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalk markings
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse lines with high-visibility continental or ladder-style markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and prevent vehicles from parking too close to the crosswalk, improving sightlines.

interventions.title: Pedestrian countdown signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time remaining.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and modern curb ramps with tactile paving in a residential setting. However, visibility is compromised by parked vehicles near the corner, and dedicated pedestrian signals are not visible at this signalized crossing.

hazards.name: Parked vehicle sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on the right side of the image may block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway along the curb

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals.
hazards.location_in_image: Main utility pole with traffic light
